newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TOO MANY SCOTS FOR BIG UEFA NIGHT AT CHARLIE'S.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOO MANY SCOTS FOR BIG UEFA NIGHT AT CHARLIE'S.

text.p: Tiny Andorran amateur club Esportiu Principat, which used to be named after a restaurant, are struggling to find room for all their guests for a big UEFA Cup night against Dundee United later this month.
Principat said on Thursday that they were looking for another stadium to stage the first preliminary round tie against the Scottish team because their current ground holds just 600 fans.
The prospect of more than 2,000 Scots descending on the tiny Andorran town of Ginebra for the match on July 23 has given the club a problem.
Principat will become the first team from the tiny principality to compete in Europe.
Formed from Andorran Real Madrid supporters, it was originally called Charlie's Restaurant before local government and sporting officials suggested they change the name.
"Dundee United will be a very tough team and what we are hoping is just to stay close to them," club vice-president Jose Pichel said. "However I hope we'll sell plenty of tickets."
One possibility is that the game will be played at Spanish first division side Espanyol whose Sarria stadium has a capacity of 41,000.
Dundee United manager Jim McLean, speaking by telephone, played down any expectations of his team setting scoring records when they face the Andorrans.
"Scottish teams have a bit of a reputation for coming unstuck against supposedly weaker teams away from home," he said. "I remember Motherwell struggled in the Faroe Islands not so long ago."
